question: Subsea power cables are vital for Europe’s energy security, both to ensure connections between Member States and the supply of offshore wind energy. At the same time, these cables are vulnerable to hybrid threats, as incidents in the Baltic Sea have shown.

The JRC is warning that repair operations could take months, due to a structural shortage of specialist cable repair vessels, which could have major consequences for electricity generation and transmission.

1 In the EU Action Plan on Cable Security of February 20252 the Commission proposed establishing a multi-purpose ‘EU Cable Vessels Reserve Fleet’, which could be deployed for emergency repairs of subsea power and data cables. There are also market-led initiatives, such as the collaboration between Prysmian and N-Sea.

3 However, industry is stressing that without concrete European action the continuity of the electricity supply is under threat.4 A public-private partnership is therefore essential to boost Europe’s offshore repair capacity, given the high costs involved in constructing cable vessels, the rising demand for maintenance and the increasing geopolitical risks.5 1.
What steps has the Commission taken since the action plan was published and what time frame does it envisage for the further development of a European reserve fleet?
How will the Commission, together with the Member States, the EU agencies, NATO and private partners, structure the administrative and operational collaboration relating to this fleet?

Have the potential sources of funding for the reserve fleet already been determined and how will they be coordinated with other maritime and energy programmes, such as the Industrial Maritime Strategy?

answer: EN E-004479/25 on behalf of the European Commission (15.1.2026) The Action Plan on Cable Security1 addresses the security of critical communication and energy submarine cables. The Commission has been consulting industry and Member States to better understand their needs regarding optical and power cables repairs.
Looking ahead, concrete project proposals for the development of regional cable hubs are expected in 2026, which will aid in improving detection and facilitate repair operations.

To structure collaboration on cable security and resilience, the Commission intends to leverage existing maritime frameworks and will integrate a multi-tier approach involving Member States, EU agencies, the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO), and private partners. The defence dimension in the hubs proposal will play a crucial role in ensuring military integration for response actions.

For optical cables, the Commission will follow up on the announced modular repair equipment capacity ready to be plugged on vessels to increase the responsiveness of the EU, in a cost-effective manner. A first pilot call is expected to be issued in 2026 under the Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) Digital programme, targeting the Baltic Sea, followed by one more CEF call open to all EU sea basins.

In addition, dedicated calls to support smart cable systems and cable projects of European interest are expected to be issued in 2026 to address the prevention and detection requirements mentioned in the Action Plan, in cooperation with the deployment of the regional cable hubs, funded via the Digital Europe Programme.

The Commission is committed to making sure that funding aligns with strategic maritime and energy objectives to support infrastructure security and resilience, and that such actions are eligible under the upcoming multiannual financial framework.
